newsitem.title: FRANCE: Idea of new world trade talk round gains - Brittan.
newsitem.headline: Idea of new world trade talk round gains - Brittan.

text.p: European Foreign Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Tuesday the idea of having a new round of world trade liberalisation negotiations at the end of the decade appeared to have "taken off with a vengeance".

Brittan said he had carried out soundings during a meeting here of ministers from the 29 OECD countries and that the idea had won favour with Mexico, Australia, New Zealand, the Czech Republic, Switzerland, Germany, France, Portugal and Britain.

"I'm very agreeably surprised to hear that this idea has taken off with a vengeance at this OECD meeting," Brittan, who represents the European Union in World Trade Organisation talks, told reporters.
He said his soundings with ministers at the two-day OECD meeting showed "dramatic, unexpected and welcome developments".
But, questioned on the U.S. position, Brittan acknowledged that Washington was still cautious.
"There's a lot of persuasion work to be done," he said. But U.S. objections were "not fundamental" ones, he added.

Earlier, Australian Minister for Trade Timothy Fischer told Reuters his country "were prepared to give it consideration, but on the understanding that agriculture comes into it -- no 'ifs' no 'buts'".
Australia is a leading member of the Cairns group of nations who are ardent promoters of farm liberalisation at world level.
Brittan said investment, intellectural property and competition issues should be brought into the talks.
